title: Nonreciprocal phonon propagation via spatially asymmetric magnon-phonon coupling
authors: Hiroyuki Moriya, Motoki Asano, Daiki Hatanaka, Yoshitaka Taniyasu, Hajime Okamoto, Hiroshi Yamaguchi
abstract: Nonreciprocal propagation of surface acoustic waves (SAWs) based on the spatial asymmetry of magnon-phonon coupling is demonstrated. This nonreciprocity is enabled by an acoustic wavelength scale thick magnetic layer formed under a thin piezoelectric film. In this configuration, magnon modes activated by dipole-dipole interactions are localized near either the top or bottom interface depending on the propagation direction of the SAW. As a result, the spatial overlap between interfacial magnon and surface phonon modes is expected to become direction dependent, in a manner that leads to distinct unidirectional propagation of SAWs. Notably, the resulting nonreciprocity reaches the highest level among those reported for SAW devices based on a single magnetic layer. This finding will establish a new strategy of nonreciprocal acoustic propagation in a structurally simple magnomechanical device.
summary: The authors report achieving significant nonreciprocal phonon propagation in a magnetic thin film device by coupling surface acoustic waves to magnon modes. This directionality is shown to stem from the spatial asymmetry of the magnon-phonon interaction, which they model using coupled wave equations. The findings establish a novel, highly efficient strategy for unidirectional acoustic energy transfer.
main_problem: The study demonstrates nonreciprocal propagation of surface acoustic waves (SAWs) by exploiting spatially asymmetric magnon-phonon coupling in a magnomechanical device.
main_result: A large, direction-dependent absorption contrast ($\Delta S$) was observed, reaching $25.2 	ext{ dB/mm}$, which is theoretically attributed to the interaction with surface-localized magnon modes.
method: The research combines experimental measurements of SAW transmission ($S_{12}, S_{21}$) using a VNA with theoretical modeling based on coupled equations of motion for phonon and magnon fields.
model_or_system: The physical platform is an AlN/YIG heterostructure, where the coupling mechanism relies on the spatial asymmetry of magnon modes localized near interfaces due to dipole-dipole interactions.
key_observables: SAW transmission spectra ($S_{12}$ and $S_{21}$) as functions of external magnetic field ($\mu_0H_{	ext{ext}}$) and angle ($\phi$); the nonreciprocity contrast $\Delta S = |S_{12} - S_{21}|$.
important_parameters: The optimal nonreciprocity is achieved at specific external magnetic fields (e.g., $4.2 	ext{ mT}$) and angles ($\phi=90^\circ$); the YIG layer thickness ($5.7 \mu	ext{m}$) is crucial.
main_assumptions: The nonreciprocity mechanism is primarily governed by coupling to surface-localized magnon modes, which exhibit an exponential decay profile along the film thickness.
figures_summary: Figures show schematic representations of asymmetric coupling (Fig. 1), device setups and baseline spectra (Fig. 2), field dependence plots showing clear directional dips in $S_{21}$ but not $S_{12}$ (Fig. 3), and color maps illustrating the angle-dependent nonreciprocity contrast $\Delta S$ (Fig. 4).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from experimental demonstration of large, direction-dependent absorption in a piezo-on-magnet system to theoretical modeling that confirms this effect arises specifically from spatially asymmetric magnon-phonon coupling involving surface modes.
why_interesting: This work provides an excellent example of engineered nonreciprocity using magnomechanics, which is highly relevant for developing quantum devices where directional control (e.g., in quantum communication or sensing) is paramount.
